- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 5–10 days of 30d window).
- Forecasts tend to peak too early or too high after recent spikes (e.g., 74–76 range), then overshoot and fail to correct downward.
- Mean reversion is underappreciated — model fails to recognize that prices often revert to lower levels after short-term spikes.
- Forecast horizon bias: 30-day forecasts show persistent overconfidence in upward momentum, ignoring recent downward trends.
- Lagged corrections: model reacts too slowly to recent price drops; true outcomes often dip below forecasted values within 5–7 days.
- Overshoot after spikes: model forecasts peak higher than true outcome after a spike, then fails to adjust downward in subsequent days.
- No clear pattern of underestimating low-range values (e.g., 65–68), but overestimates mid-range (70–74) and high-range (75+) values.
- Model exhibits “sticky” behavior — once a price rises, it tends to hold or rise further, even when data suggests mean reversion.
